cards.text: Abner, the commander of Saul's army, just offered to bring all Israel over to David, and David sent him away in peace (2 Samuel 2:8; 3:21). Just then, Joab, the leader of David's soldiers, gets back from a raid with a great plunder (2 Samuel 2:13). But Abner's already gone.
When Joab and his troops arrive, somebody fills him in: Abner son of Ner came to see the king, and the king sent him on his way in peace. Friend, nothing good EVER follows “while you were out.”

cards.question: Joab hears Abner came and went in peace. Joab goes straight to King David. What does Joab do?

answers.text: Demands to know why David let Abner go
Thanks David for making peace with Abner
Hands David the plunder from the raid

cards.text: Here's Joab, to the king's face: “What have you done? Look, Abner came to you. Why did you dismiss him? Now he is getting away!” To the KING! A shiny new stamper took my spot on the counter, and I didn't say ONE word.

cards.question: Joab tells King David what Abner was really up to. What does Joab claim Abner came to do?

answers.text: Deceive David and track his movements
Make peace and serve David as king
Challenge Joab to a fight in Hebron

cards.text: As soon as Joab leaves David, he sends messengers after Abner, and they bring him back from the well of Sirah. Friend, nothing good ever happens after “can you come back real quick?”

cards.question: King David knows Joab sent messengers to bring Abner back.

cards.text: Abner comes back to Hebron. Joab pulls him aside into the gateway, as if to speak to him privately.

cards.question: In the gateway at Hebron, what does Joab do to Abner?
The text tells us why Joab stabs Abner: Abner died on account of the blood of Joab's brother ___.

cards.text: Afterward, the news reaches David. And the king has something to say.

cards.question: When David hears that Joab killed Abner, what does David say about himself and his kingdom?

answers.text: They are forever guiltless before the LORD
They owe Joab their thanks for this
They are safer now that Abner is gone

cards.question: Next, David asks the LORD to forgive Joab and his father's house.

cards.text: Instead, David says may it whirl over the head of Joab and his father's whole house, and may they never be without someone with a discharge or skin disease, someone who leans on a staff, falls by the sword or lacks food. Friend, that is NOT a slap on the wrist.

cards.question: The writer says Joab murdered Abner on his own, with no one else involved.
Joab and his brother Abishai murdered Abner because Abner killed their brother Asahel. Where did Abner kill Asahel?

cards.text: Abner is dead. Now David gives orders to Joab and all the people with him.

cards.question: After Abner's murder, what does King David order Joab and all the people with him to do?

answers.text: Tear their clothes and mourn Abner

cards.text: David's words: “Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn before Abner.” And Joab's in that crowd too. I bet that sackcloth felt REAL heavy on him.

cards.question: King David himself walks behind Abner's funeral bier.

cards.text: They bury Abner in Hebron. The king stands at the tomb.

cards.question: At Abner's tomb in Hebron, what does King David do?

cards.text: Then the king sings a lament for Abner, and it opens with a question: “Should Abner die the death of a fool?”

cards.question: In his lament, David sings that Abner's hands were not bound and his feet were not fettered. So how does David say Abner fell?

answers.text: As a man falls before the wicked
As a soldier falls in battle
As a traitor falls in judgment

cards.text: All the people weep over Abner even more. Then they come and urge David to eat something while it's still day. Friend, if somebody urged ME to eat a cookie, it'd be gone before they finished the sentence.

cards.question: The people urge David to eat something while it's still day. What does David do?

answers.text: Swears not to eat before sunset
Eats with the people to comfort them
Eats a little to keep his strength

cards.question: The people take note of how David handles Abner's death, and they are unhappy with it.
On that day, all the troops and all Israel were ___ that the king had no part in the murder of Abner.

cards.text: Then the king turns to his servants with a question about the man they just buried.

cards.question: Speaking to his servants, what does King David say has fallen today in Israel?

cards.text: Then David gets honest: he is weak this day, though anointed as king, and these men, the sons of Zeruiah, are too fierce for him. That's Joab and his brother Abishai (2 Samuel 2:18). An anointed king admitting he's outmatched. Friend, I used to lose arguments to the rubber bands I shared that junk drawer with.

cards.question: After saying the sons of Zeruiah are too fierce for him, what does David ask of the LORD?

answers.text: Repay the evildoer according to his evil
Give David the strength to punish them
Show mercy to the sons of Zeruiah

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave David for now. Trust me, friend, this story is FAR from finished.

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 2 quotes "while you were out.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card calls Joab "the leader of David's soldiers" and cites 2 Samuel 2:13. That verse only says Joab son of Zeruiah and David's servants went out. It never calls him their leader, so the reference doesn't support the fact.

rule.text: References. Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: "Nothing good EVER follows 'while you were out'" tells the baker that Joab's reaction is negative. That rules out the wrong answer "Thanks David for making peace with Abner" on card 3.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Outside the quote, the card has three sentences: "Here's Joab, to the king's face: …", "To the KING!" and the stamper joke.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke uses the same template as card 2 ("Friend, nothing good ever happens after '…'") only four cards later. That makes the humor feel formulaic. It also foreshadows harm right before the card 9 question.

rule.text: No formula. His personality fits whatever moment he's in, whether it's a tense moment in a story, a hard teaching or a quick question. There are no joke quotas and no required kinds of jokes.

findings.problem: Outside the quote, the card has three sentences: "David's words: …", "And Joab's in that crowd too." and "I bet that sackcloth felt REAL heavy on him."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card has three sentences and carries two passage beats: the people weeping more (v34) and the people urging David to eat (v35).

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The joke "if somebody urged ME to eat a cookie, it'd be gone before they finished the sentence" sets Papa Dorin against David. That signals David won't eat, which rules out the wrong answers "Eats with the people to comfort them" and "Eats a little to keep his strength" on card 10. A food joke also lands right as all the people weep over Abner even more, which doesn't fit the moment.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The card has four sentences and carries two beats: David's admission and the identification of the sons of Zeruiah. It also adds a joke on top.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The story-continues line nearly copies the doc's example ("And that's where we'll leave it for now. Trust me, friend, this story's not done.") instead of being written fresh.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The card is only the story-continues line and tells no verse, but it cites 2 Samuel 3:39. That verse was already cited by cards 15 and 16.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the story-continues line, which verses should it cite: the passage's last verse, nothing, or something else?
